rationale:
This slate follows the growth playbook. Today's one long-form is the Lane A hair-loss redo, the top priority. It catches viewers from the 1,016-view "Will It Grow Back?" Short, and it is an evergreen deep-dive that rests on settled evidence: Gupta 2026 (5.4% vs 0.9%), the label's figures (7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men) and dermatology sources on telogen effluvium. The new Cureus semaglutide meta-analysis appears only as separate class context.

The three Shorts fill the playbook's slots:
- **08:00, body-worry reassurance:** tirzepatide injection site reactions, a fresh "is this normal?" fear (proven median about 104) with a new fact from the Cureus meta-analysis.
- **13:00, lead:** the retatrutide TRIUMPH-4 knee-pain "what's confirmed?" Short with a loop ending. Retatrutide Phase 3 is a proven peak format, and this trial hasn't been used. I skipped the retatrutide sleep apnea idea because those NEJM trials already ran as a Short on 10-24. I also skipped retatrutide vs tirzepatide because it is peaking and overlaps the 10-29 long and the dysesthesia Short.
- **20:00, funnel (Exp D):** a protein breakfast when appetite is low. It points to the live What to Eat and Protein long-forms.

The spin-off rule clashes with the playbook. The shared rule asks for a Short that spins off today's long-form, but the playbook bans hair Shorts this week. I followed the playbook. The two existing hair Shorts ("Will It Grow Back?" and "How Common Is It") act as L1's feeders instead. The publisher adds L1's link to line 1 of both descriptions once L1 is verified live.

Other choices:
- **Kept out:** the stopping, fatigue, birth control and dehydration long-forms wait for later days in the queue. The "sick on tirzepatide" and birth control topics are marked caution, so they need a long, evidence-first treatment, not a Short.
- **Spread:** no pillar is used more than twice. Body systems are hair, skin at the injection site, knee joints and nutrition.
- **Safety lines:** every piece carries "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line. Side-effect pieces also carry "don't stop or change your medicines on your own".

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common shedding was in the trials, why it happens (telogen effluvium linked to rapid weight loss), when it typically starts and regrows, why women report it more often, what helps, and when to see a doctor or dermatologist
pieces.angle: Keep the plan as written, with one change: drop chapter 5's Cureus figures unless the scriptwriter can open the paper and find 191/11,564 vs 36/9,799 printed in it. If they can't, replace chapter 5 with a verified 2026 class source. One option is Taj et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2026 (doi 10.1111/dom.70382). Another is the STEP/SURMOUNT comparison: about 3% on semaglutide and about 5% on tirzepatide vs about 1% on placebo, across separate trials, not head-to-head, credited to the source that prints those numbers. Say 'a related medicine, separate trials'. Credit telogen effluvium timing to the AAD or DermNet page and give it as typical ranges, not predictions. Thumbnail: 'Usually Grows Back'.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Hair Loss: Will It Grow Back?
pieces.why: Priority 1 in the playbook. A Lane A long-form here gives the 1,016-view hair Short somewhere to send viewers and is backed by strong trial and label evidence. The two existing hair Shorts (not new ones, because hair Shorts are banned this week) act as its feeders once the link is added. | fact-check: This is a high-value Lane A redo and the science is sound. Gupta et al., Science Progress 2026 reports hair loss in 5.4% of people on tirzepatide vs 0.9% on placebo in pooled weight-loss trials, and I confirmed that through secondary reporting. The label figure (7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men) comes from the craft notes, which were already checked. The structure, hedges and safety lines meet the playbook. One problem: I could not confirm that chapter 5's 'Cureus semaglutide RCT meta-analysis (191/11,564 vs 36/9,799, low certainty)' exists. The only 2026 Cureus semaglutide meta-analysis I found says alopecia events were too rare and too inconsistently reported to pool. That contradicts the planned figures. A L1 that credits numbers to a source that doesn't say them is exactly the kind of failure that held L1 10-30. Other notes: give telogen effluvium timing from a dermatology source (AAD or DermNet), as averages: shedding usually starts about 2–4 months after the trigger and regrowth takes months. In the thumbnail, keep 'Usually' in the hedge.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: redness, itching or a small lump. What's normal, what the label reports, and when to call
pieces.angle: Answer within 10 s: mild redness, itching or a small bump where you injected was reported in the trials and is usually mild. Use the current Zepbound label's injection-site reaction rates exactly as printed: every dose arm vs placebo, with the label's own list of included terms (bruising, redness, itching, pain, rash). For the new fact, use a verified source: either the label's hypersensitivity figures (5% vs 3% on placebo; immediate reactions 2.1% vs 0.4%) or Taj et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2026, saying injection-site reactions were most often reported with tirzepatide among GLP-1 medicines and were dose-related. Drop the Cureus 156/5,066 figures unless the paper is opened and the numbers are found printed in it. Credit site rotation only to the Instructions for Use. Red flags: spreading redness, warmth or pus means calling your prescriber. Swelling of the face, lips or throat, or trouble breathing, means emergency care (label wording). Keep the Exp F line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'.
pieces.why: Proven calm body-worry 'is this normal?' format (median about 104) on a fresh fear we haven't covered, with a new meta-analysis fact. It also tests demand for the planned injection-site long-form. | fact-check: The topic is a good body-worry reassurance fit. The Zepbound label reports injection site reactions in about 6–8% of people (by dose) vs about 2% on placebo, and hypersensitivity reactions in about 5% vs 3%. I could not verify the 'new fact': a 2026 Cureus semaglutide meta-analysis with injection-site reactions at 156/5,066 vs 114/3,483 and very low certainty. The closest Cureus 2026 review I found doesn't match that description, and crediting it unverified is a hold risk. It's also semaglutide-only context in a tirzepatide Short. A better-sourced new fact comes from the label itself or Taj et al., DOM 2026: injection site reactions were dose-related and were reported most often with tirzepatide (about 2–7%) among GLP-1 medicines.

pieces.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain: TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 (445 adults with overweight or obesity and knee osteoarthritis, 68 weeks, vs placebo), now in fuller publication
pieces.angle: Lead with TRIUMPH-4 from Lilly's December 11, 2025 release, called a 'company topline result, not yet peer-reviewed' unless a TRIUMPH-4 journal paper is found and opened. 445 adults with overweight or obesity and knee osteoarthritis, 9 mg or 12 mg vs placebo, 68 weeks. On 12 mg, WOMAC knee pain fell 75.8% on average. In a post-hoc analysis, 12.0% on 12 mg (about 1 in 8) and 14.1% on 9 mg were completely free of knee pain, vs 4.2% on placebo. Don't merge this with the separate TRIUMPH-1 NEJM knee subgroup (80 weeks, up to 61.6% pain reduction). If it's mentioned at all, call it 'a separate, larger trial, now peer-reviewed in NEJM'. Weight-and-knee-load line as a leading explanation: 'likely partly because'. Copy one per-arm discontinuation line exactly from the release. Status: investigational, not approved anywhere as of November 2, 2026; Lilly plans to submit in Q1 2027, and a submission isn't approval. Tirzepatide knee data: separate trials, not head-to-head. No sources, only 'ask a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials'. Exp F line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line, then a loop back to the opening question.
pieces.working_title: Retatrutide and Knee Pain: What's Confirmed?
pieces.why: New retatrutide Phase 3 data is a proven 13:00 peak format (273/206/122 views). TRIUMPH-4 is fresh in publication coverage, and knee pain is a benefit-beyond-weight angle we haven't used. | fact-check: The TRIUMPH-4 core facts check out: 445 adults with overweight or obesity and knee osteoarthritis, retatrutide 9 mg or 12 mg vs placebo, 68 weeks, and up to 28.7% weight loss on 12 mg. WOMAC pain fell 75.8% on 12 mg. Completely free of knee pain at week 68: 14.1% on 9 mg and 12.0% on 12 mg vs 4.2% on placebo. That pain-free figure was described as a post-hoc analysis, so label it. 'About 1 in 8' is accurate for the 12 mg arm only. Don't say 'on retatrutide', because the 9 mg arm was higher. Lilly's planned Q1 2027 US submission is confirmed. Big problem: I could not confirm the claim that TRIUMPH-4 is 'now in fuller publication'. The October 2026 NEJM paper (doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2604169) is TRIUMPH-1, an 80-week trial with a knee OA subgroup of 574. Its WOMAC results are different: up to 61.6% pain reduction and 25% weight loss on 12 mg. Mixing the two trials would be a factual error. Unless a TRIUMPH-4 peer-reviewed paper is found, the TRIUMPH-4 figures come from Lilly's December 11, 2025 topline release and must be called 'not yet peer-reviewed'.

pieces.topic: Breakfast on tirzepatide when you're barely hungry: why a small, protein-forward breakfast helps, with 2 concrete examples
pieces.angle: Question: 'Not hungry in the morning on tirzepatide? Do you still need breakfast?' Honest answer: there's no rule that you must eat breakfast. But when appetite is low all day, a small protein-forward breakfast is one easy way to get closer to enough protein. Credit only 'get enough protein' (and, where relevant, the nausea tip about the first few days) to the 2025 ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS joint advisory. 'Protein food first', small portions and eating slowly are our own tips, with no tag. Two examples, with 'grams vary by brand, check the label': a small pot of plain Greek yogurt (about 15–20 grams of protein, per the label) or 2 eggs (about 12 grams, per the label/USDA). Kidney caveat: 'If you have kidney disease, ask your clinician how much protein is right for you.' One GI line: if food sits heavily or nausea is bad, smaller and blander portions may sit better; persistent vomiting or severe belly pain means calling your prescriber. No calorie or restriction talk. 'Not personal advice' plus the prescriber line. No Exp F line. Last line: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.'
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Breakfast When You're Not Hungry
pieces.why: Exp D funnel to the live What to Eat and Protein long-forms (Protein had our fastest Lane A start). It rides the EatingWell breakfast story from Nov 1. | fact-check: This is a safe, useful funnel topic for What to Eat and Protein. The 2025 joint advisory (ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS, Mozaffarian et al.) supports eating enough protein and nutrient-dense foods while on GLP-1 medicines. Per the craft notes, its quotable content is enough protein, strength training at least 3 times a week, and avoiding fatty or high-fibre foods in the first few days to ease nausea. I could not confirm that it says 'eat your protein food first', and nothing suggests it says to eat breakfast. Credit only what it prints. Framing: the answer must not tell people to eat when they aren't hungry as a rule, or suggest that skipping breakfast is harmful. Present it as one option for hitting daily protein when appetite is low. Gram counts must come from a food label and be phrased 'about, as on the label', because they vary by brand. Avoid calorie talk, as planned.
